text: Now Absalom, David's son, had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and in time David's son Amnon fell in love with her.
Amnon was so tormented over his sister Tamar that he made himself sick, for she was a virgin and it seemed impossible for him to do anything about it.
But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
Jonadab asked him, why do you look so worn out morning after morning, son of the king? Won't you tell me? Amnon told him he was in love with Tamar, his brother Absalom's sister.

Jonadab said, lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send your sister Tamar to fix food for you in your sight, so you can watch her and eat from her own hand.
So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill; when the king came to see him, Amnon asked him to let his sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in his sight, so he could eat from her hand.
David sent word to Tamar at the palace: go to your brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him.
Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down; she took dough, kneaded it, shaped it into cakes in his sight, and baked them.
She took the pan and served him, but he refused to eat and told everyone to leave the room; so they all went out.
Then Amnon told Tamar to bring the food into his bedroom so he could eat from her hand; Tamar took the cakes she had made and carried them in to her brother Amnon.
But when she brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, come, lie with me, my sister.
She answered, no, my brother, do not force me; such a thing should not be done in Israel. Do not do this outrageous thing.
Where could I ever get rid of my shame? And you would become like one of the wicked fools in Israel. Please, speak to the king; he will not refuse to let me marry you.
But he would not listen to her, and being stronger than she was, he forced her and raped her.
Then Amnon hated her with an intense hatred; in fact he hated her now more than he had loved her before, and he said to her, get up and get out!
No, she said, sending me away now would be a greater wrong than what you already did to me. But he refused to listen to her.
He called his personal servant and said, get this woman out of my sight and bolt the door behind her.
So the servant put her out and bolted the door after her. She was wearing a long robe with sleeves, the kind of garment the king's virgin daughters wore.
Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the ornamented robe she had on, put her hand on her head, and went away weeping loudly as she went.

Her brother Absalom asked her, has Amnon your brother been with you? For now, my sister, be quiet; he is your brother, don't take this to heart. So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.
When King David heard about all this, he was furious.
Absalom never said a word to Amnon, good or bad, because he hated him for violating his sister Tamar.
Two full years later, Absalom had sheepshearers working at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, and he invited all the king's sons.
Absalom went to the king and said, your servant has sheepshearers at work; would the king and his officials please come along with your servant?
The king replied, no, my son, we shouldn't all go, or we'll be too much of a burden to you. Although Absalom urged him, the king still would not go, though he gave him his blessing.
Then Absalom said, if not, then please let my brother Amnon come with us. The king asked him, why should he go with you?
But Absalom kept urging him until he let Amnon and all the rest of the king's sons go with him.
Absalom ordered his men, watch for when Amnon is merry with wine, and when I tell you to strike him down, do it. Don't be afraid; haven't I myself given you this command? Be strong and brave.
So Absalom's men did to Amnon exactly what Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's other sons got up, mounted their mules, and fled.
While they were still on the road, word reached David that Absalom had struck down all the king's sons and not one of them was left.
The king got up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; all his servants who were standing nearby also tore their clothes.

But Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah, said, my lord should not think all the young men, the king's sons, are dead. Only Amnon is dead, for this has been Absalom's fixed plan ever since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
So my lord the king should not take the report to heart, thinking all the king's sons are dead; only Amnon is dead.
Meanwhile Absalom had fled. The young man on watch looked up and saw a large crowd coming down the road on the hillside behind him.
Jonadab said to the king, look, the king's sons are coming; it has happened just as your servant said.
As soon as he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived, weeping loudly; the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, while David mourned for his son every day.
After Absalom fled to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
And once King David had finished grieving over Amnon's death, his heart longed to go out to Absalom.
